einzeiler: The legal battle surrounding Weev and the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act appeal.
kurzfassung: Andrew Auernheimer, known as Weev, faced conviction under the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act for accessing AT&T servers and obtaining user email addresses. His defense attorney, Tor Ekeland, took on the case pro bono while managing immense personal and financial strain. Ultimately, an appeal led by Ekeland and legal experts resulted in the conviction being vacated on venue grounds.
stichpunkte: Andrew Auernheimer was convicted on identity fraud and unauthorized computer access charges following the AT&T server breach.
Defense attorney Tor Ekeland struggled financially and personally while representing Auernheimer pro bono.
The tragic suicide of Aaron Swartz brought renewed public attention and support to computer crime law reform and the appeal.
The Electronic Frontier Foundation and legal scholar Orin Kerr joined the appeal team, challenging the definition of unauthorized access.
During oral arguments, the appeals court shifted focus to the issue of venue, questioning why the trial was held in New Jersey.
The Third Circuit Court of Appeals agreed that New Jersey was an improper venue, vacating the conviction.
Following his release from prison, Auernheimer fled the United States and continued his trolling activities abroad.
Subsequent Supreme Court rulings and DOJ policy updates eventually narrowed the application of the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act.

clips.text: An individual possesses undeniable intellect but maintains an irredeemable reputation for deceit, rendering all claims untrustworthy.
Trial law requires high-stakes courtroom experience that cannot be replicated through observation or preparation.
A customer who changes clothes to meet a dress code after initially being turned away has not committed trespassing.
The constitutional requirement for trial location originated as a safeguard against the British crown transporting radicals across distances.
An overexpanded law enforcement apparatus creates elastic statutes to manufacture crimes simply to sustain itself.

beschreibung:
The Electronic Frontier Foundation, long time critics of the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act, followed Weev's trial - but did not get involved. For the appeal, however, the organization decided to step it. But althought the EFF had some strong points against the CFAA - the justices, appearntly, had something very different on their mind.
